microtheory.name: basal_ganglia_circuit
microtheory.definition: Basal ganglia as action-selection + reinforcement-learning engine. Cortex → striatum → globus pallidus → thalamus → cortex loop. Direct + indirect pathways implement go/no-go decisions. Dopamine from VTA/SNc modulates striatal plasticity, encoding reward prediction error. This is the neural substrate of habit, skill, addiction, parkinsonism. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec dispatch + reinforcement of which corrections to fire.

concepts.name: striatum
concepts.definition: Largest basal ganglia component. Input region. Two subdivisions: dorsal (caudate + putamen) for action; ventral (nucleus accumbens) for motivation + reward. ~95% medium spiny neurons. Substrate analogue: the input layer of ActionSpec selection.

concepts.name: globus_pallidus
concepts.definition: Two subnuclei: GPi (internal) is the output; GPe (external) is part of the indirect pathway. Tonically active inhibition of thalamus that the striatum gates. Substrate analogue: default-inhibition that ActionSpec firing must overcome.

concepts.name: substantia_nigra
concepts.definition: Midbrain. SNc (pars compacta) — dopamine neurons sending to striatum. SNr (pars reticulata) — GABAergic output similar to GPi. Lesion of SNc = Parkinson's. Substrate analogue: source of the reward-modulation signal.

concepts.name: ventral_tegmental_area
concepts.definition: Midbrain dopamine source for the mesolimbic + mesocortical pathways. Reward, motivation, addiction. Substrate analogue: source of plasticity-modulation for the substrate's ActionSpec coverage.

concepts.name: subthalamic_nucleus
concepts.definition: Small but critical relay in the indirect pathway. Excites GPi to prevent unwanted actions. Deep brain stimulation target for Parkinson's. Substrate analogue: action-prevention concepts in the substrate's action selection.

concepts.name: medium_spiny_neuron
concepts.definition: Striatum's primary neuron. GABAergic. Two main classes: D1-receptor-expressing (direct pathway) + D2-receptor-expressing (indirect pathway). Their balance determines action selection. Substrate analogue: positive vs negative ActionSpec coverage attrs.

concepts.name: direct_pathway
concepts.definition: Striatum (D1) → GPi/SNr → thalamus → cortex. Disinhibits thalamus when activated; net effect: GO. Dopamine enhances D1 activity, biasing toward action. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec firing.

concepts.name: indirect_pathway
concepts.definition: Striatum (D2) → GPe → STN → GPi/SNr → thalamus → cortex. Net effect: NO-GO (inhibition strengthened). Dopamine REDUCES D2 activity, removing the brake. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec rejection / blockade.

concepts.name: hyperdirect_pathway
concepts.definition: Cortex → STN → GPi. Fast, generic 'stop' signal that aborts incipient actions. Substrate analogue: emergency abort mechanism for incorrect ActionSpec dispatches.

concepts.name: dopaminergic_rpe_signal
concepts.definition: Schultz 1997. Dopamine neurons fire above baseline when outcome > expectation, below baseline when outcome < expectation. Encodes reward prediction error — the teaching signal for striatal plasticity. Substrate analogue: ΔF signal driving ActionSpec weight updates.

concepts.name: striatal_plasticity
concepts.definition: Cortico-striatal synapses follow Hebbian + dopamine-gated rules. Active corticostriatal synapses strengthen when dopamine spikes (positive RPE) and weaken when it dips (negative RPE). Substrate analogue: ActionSpec covers_correction strengthening when corrections succeed.

concepts.name: actor_critic_architecture
concepts.definition: Sutton + Barto's RL framework maps onto basal ganglia: dorsal striatum = actor (selects actions); ventral striatum = critic (evaluates states); dopamine = TD error signal between them. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec dispatcher + assessment cortex co-evolving via mutual updating.

concepts.name: temporal_difference_learning
concepts.definition: Sutton 1988. Update value estimates based on the difference between successive predictions: V(s_t) += α · [r + γV(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)]. Dopamine encodes exactly this TD error. Substrate analogue: F_t+1 - F_t in the substrate's frustration dynamics.

concepts.name: habit_formation
concepts.definition: Repeated action-outcome pairings under reward shift control from prefrontal (deliberative) to dorsolateral striatum (habitual). Habits are fast, automatic, insensitive to outcome devaluation. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec usage growing into a default-fire from sustained successful firing history.

concepts.name: action_selection
concepts.definition: When multiple actions are simultaneously possible, basal ganglia gates ONE through by disinhibiting its thalamo-cortical loop while keeping others inhibited. Winner-take-all over actions. Substrate analogue: the substrate's runtime_discovery selecting which FilterSpec/ActionSpec to fire given an event.

concepts.name: goal_directed_versus_habit
concepts.definition: Two parallel systems for behaviour: goal-directed (outcome-sensitive, slow, prefrontal-ventral-striatal) and habitual (stimulus-response, fast, dorsolateral-striatal). They compete. Substrate analogue: deliberate ArchitectureCortex-driven correction vs FilterSpec auto-dispatch.

concepts.name: exploration_versus_exploitation
concepts.definition: Dopamine tonic level shifts the explore-exploit balance. High tonic = explore; low tonic = exploit known good actions. Substrate analogue: curiosity-drive amplitude modulation.

concepts.name: parkinsonism
concepts.definition: Degeneration of SNc dopamine neurons → striatal dopamine depletion → indirect pathway over-active → action initiation impaired (bradykinesia, tremor, rigidity). Levodopa replacement helps. Substrate analogue: what failure mode of the substrate would look like if its action_dispatch couldn't fire.

concepts.name: huntington_disease
concepts.definition: Striatal medium spiny neurons degenerate (D2 first, then D1). Indirect pathway fails, then direct → uncontrolled movements (chorea), eventually rigidity. Substrate analogue: failure of action-inhibition before action-initiation.

concepts.name: addiction_dysregulation
concepts.definition: Repeated drug-induced dopamine spikes hijack the striatal learning signal, over-strengthening drug-related cue-action associations. Substrate analogue: a buggy reward signal training the wrong ActionSpec to fire.

rules.name: basal_ganglia_select_actions_by_disinhibition
rules.head: multiple ActionSpecs are eligible for firing
rules.body: the basal ganglia analog (direct vs indirect pathway balance) selects ONE by disinhibiting its loop while keeping others suppressed. The substrate's runtime_discovery dispatch implements this — competition + selection.

rules.name: dopamine_encodes_reward_prediction_error
rules.head: an action outcome differs from expectation
rules.body: the substrate's analog of dopamine (the ΔF signal) modulates the strength of the ActionSpec→event association. Better-than-expected outcomes strengthen; worse weaken. This is Sutton+Barto TD learning.

rules.name: habits_form_through_repetition
rules.head: an ActionSpec fires successfully repeatedly
rules.body: the substrate's analog of dorsal-striatal habit learning transfers control from deliberate (cortex-mediated) to automatic. The action becomes default behaviour, outcome-insensitive. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec dispatch frequency growing into a default fire.

rules.name: actor_and_critic_co_train
rules.head: an outcome is evaluated
rules.body: the actor (ActionSpec dispatcher) updates its action policy; the critic (assessment cortex) updates its value estimate. The TD error coordinates them via the dopamine analog. Two-system architecture.

rules.name: explore_exploit_balance_via_tonic_dopamine
rules.head: the substrate is in an exploration-favoring state
rules.body: the analog of tonic dopamine is elevated, biasing toward novel ActionSpec dispatch; low tonic biases toward repeating known-good ActionSpecs. Substrate analogue: curiosity-drive amplitude as exploration parameter.
